title: Reverse a backwards-running three-phase conveyor motor by swapping two supply leads
instruction: This conveyor's motor was just replaced and now runs backwards. Change which socket each supply lead is plugged into so that the conveyor runs the way the arrows on its guard point, with every plug pushed fully home, then let go. The supply is isolated; it is switched on once you are clear.
context: Electricians and motor repairers (O*NET 47-2111, 49-2092) correct a new motor's direction by exchanging any two of its three supply leads; moving all three one terminal along keeps the phase sequence and changes nothing. Here the leads start in colour order, so tidying them changes nothing either.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); everything except the leads and the tote is fixed (screwed or taped down). Terminal box: blue-grey painted box 6 (x) x 18 (y) x 4.5 cm tall, front face at x 36, centred on y 0, standing on the table. In its front face, at table level, three sockets 22 mm wide x 19 mm tall x 26 mm deep, centred at y +5 (U), 0 (V) and -5 (W). Motor: blue-grey cylinder 8 cm across and 14 cm long, axis along y, centred at x 46, y 0, resting on the table behind the box. Gearbox: dark grey block 6 x 6 x 8 cm tall at x 43 to 49, y -9 to -15, coupled to the motor; on its front face a white pointer disc 5 cm across with a red stripe from its centre to the top; a shaft from its back into the conveyor. Conveyor: light grey bed 10 (x) x 40 (y) x 5 cm tall centred at x 63, y 0, with a black belt on top; along its front a yellow guard plate 5 x 40 cm, 5.2 cm tall (x 53 to 58), carrying two black arrows pointing to the robot's right (-y), a red line across it at y +6 and a green line at y -6. Tote: blue box 6 (x) x 8 (y) x 4 cm, 150 g, on the belt centred at y 0. Gland plate: dark grey block 3 x 16 x 3 cm tall at x 12 to 15, centred on y 0. Leads: three 6 mm round PVC leads 24 cm long, brown (L1), black (L2) and grey (L3), leaving the gland plate's back face at y +5, 0 and -5, each ending in a plug body 55 x 16 x 14 mm (ABS, the lead's colour, 15 g) lying flat; brown is pushed 24 mm into U, black into V, grey into W. Each lead lies on the table in a bow to the left: it leaves the gland heading straight forward (+x), swings out to 6.4 cm left of its gland position about 8 cm from the gland, and comes back to enter its socket straight. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler and a photo; each plug carries tape marks 8 mm and 15 mm from its tip. A plug is in a socket when it is lined up with it (centre within 8 mm of the socket's centre line sideways, pointing into it within 25.8 degrees, its centre at most 5 mm above the opening's top) and its 8 mm mark is inside the face; it is home when its 15 mm mark is inside too. Score 0 unless all of: the robot has touched a plug or lead (sim: a robot point within 2 mm) at some point; no part of either robot is within 20 mm of the terminal box, the gland or any lead (plug or cable); no plug moved more than 1 mm over the last second; each plug is in a different socket; and the order reverses the motor: two leads exchanged relative to the start (an odd permutation; the start order and its two cyclic shifts score 0). Then 1.0 if all three plugs are home and the tote has run wholly past the green (forward) line (100 mm forward); otherwise 0.5. The supply is off at the start; once the robot has touched a plug or lead, it comes on whenever the robot has been clear, the plugs still and all three home for 1 s, and goes off if that stops holding; the motor then runs forward for an odd order and backward for an even one, moving the tote at 0.1 m/s; with a plug not home it does not start. The trial ends early once the score has been 1.0 for 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the three plugs out, push brown into U, black into V and grey into W until the 15 mm mark is hidden (24 mm in), lay each lead in its bow to the left as in the setup, bring the tote back to the centre of the belt between the lines, and turn the disc's stripe to the top. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: The motor is not simulated electrically: its direction is computed from the lead order (odd permutation of the start = forward, even = backward) and the tester drives the tote as a slider at 0.1 m/s, only with all three plugs home. Leads: 12 rigid 2 cm segments, no twist, fully plastic (no restoring force; they keep any shape they are left in). Plugs are rigid boxes held by the socket walls and friction (no contacts or latch); sockets 22 x 19 mm for a 16 x 14 mm plug. Drive and gland fixed.
